findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that a sanitizer bucket in the meat department was not registering levels of quaternary ammonium (0ppm). PIC investigated and found that the source of the sanitizing solution, a hose dispenser from the meat department triple sink, was using hot water, which deactivates the sanitizer in the solution. PIC determined that there was a plumbing issue that was causing hot water to come out of the dispenser without an option to make it cold. A plumber was contacted and arrived during the inspection. In the meantime, the meat department will source its sanitizing solution for surfaces and warewashing from the working sanitizer dispenser from the triple sink in the neighboring deli department. The new sanitizer bucket measured at 200pm for quaternary ammonium. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions are sanitizing at safe and effective concentrations, which is between 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium, and that sanitizing solutions are created per manufacturer’s instructions.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that the rotisserie chicken in the display warmer was hot holding at a temperature of 108 F, below the necessary 135 F. CORRECTED: PIC investigated and noted that the warming unit was turned off but the lights were turned on. PIC voluntarily discarded all rotisserie chickens that were in the display warmer. Ensure that foods that are hot held are kept at temperatures 135 F or above.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed an accumulation of dust and soil residues on nonfood-contact surfaces that could potentially contaminate food-contact surfaces:
(i) the walls and floors in the dry goods storage in the deli department in the back room near the stairs.
(ii) the ceiling ventilation in the meat department.
(iii) the caulking behind the triple sinks.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the stalls in the women’s restroom did not have covered receptacles for sanitary napkins et. al. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles for hygiene purposes and to prevent feminine hygiene products from being disposed of in the toilets.
findings.citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that 3 mops in the dish area of the deli department were not air-drying properly, siting on top of a hard surface that was not the mop sink where they cannot air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mops so that they can air-dry and drain above the mop sink. PIC also instructed staff to discard an older mop head that was not attached to a mop that had been in the same area. Ensure that mops are allowed to air-dry in a location where they cannot contaminate walls, equipment or supplies.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed both hand washing sinks in the deli and meat department did not have paper towels. During the inspection paper towel rolls were brought to the hand washing sinks. After discussing long-term solutions, the store manager gave the deli manager keys to the dispensers so that they can re-fill the rolls. The inspector also recommends posting signs around the hand washing sinks to remind employees that they must re-fill the dispensers when they are emptied. Ensure that paper towels are always available at every hand washing sink for the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed there was ice and food debris in the deli hand washing sink closest to the sushi station. The PIC was instructed to educate employees that hand washing sinks cannot be used as dump sinks. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for purposes other than hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed various single-use articles stored on the floor at the back of the deli by the staircase. The PIC will be educating employees that single-use articles must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground. Ensure that single-use items are stored properly by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) The deli walk-in cooler floor underneath the shelving. 

(2) The shelving in the meat department walk-in cooler. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed both hand washing sinks in the deli and the back hand washing sink at the meat department did not have paper towels. During the inspection paper towel rolls were brought to the hand washing sinks. Ensure that paper towels are always available at every hand washing sink for the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed the following in the deli walk-in cooler were missing date marking: (1) Container of taco meat cooked on Saturday; and (2) Container of pasta salad prepared on Thursday. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed a large container of unpackaged flour in the deli was not labeled. All easily mistakable foods (ex. white powders) not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that the flour container is properly labeled by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the caulking at the spay nozzle sink in the deli (directly to the right of the fryers) is deteriorating. The sink must be re-caulked to remove the gap between the sink and the wall. Ensure that the spray nozzle sink is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the floor underneath the fryers in the deli has an accumulation of food debris and grease. The equipment should be pulled out to facilitate deep cleaning underneath. Ensure that underneath the fryers is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the left hand washing sink (closest to the sushi station) in the deli did not have paper towels when the inspector arrived. The inspector educated the deli PIC on the importance of having paper towels available for the proper hand washing procedure. The deli PIC re-filled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Ensure there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment:
The following improper hand washing sink uses were observed during the inspection: 

(1) Observed multiple deli employees dumping buckets into hand washing sinks. The inspector educated the deli PIC about the importance of dumping liquids into the designated dump sink not hand washing sinks. 
(2) Observed a meat department employee filling up a sanitizer bucket in the hand washing sink. The employee was educated when the action was observed and they filled the remainder of the bucket in the triple sink. 

Both of the department PIC’s were instructed to educate employees on the proper hand sink usage to ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed that portions of the salad bar are not holding food temperatures at 41F or below. The side closest to the coffee station is holding all foods at 41F or below. The opposite side (closest to the hot wing station) is not holding all temperatures at 41F of below. The areas not holding food at the proper temperature are from the far left side all the way to the lettuce. The following internal temperatures were recorded: chicken 55F, lettuce 50F, green peppers 53F, cheese 54F, and ham 55F. The deli PIC and store manger were instructed to use time-as-control for the temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the cooler. The foods being temperature controlled are lettuce, mozzarella cheese, blue cheese, feta cheese, chicken, ham, turkey, crab, and eggs. The rest of the non-TCS foods are allowed to remain in the cooler all day. Since all foods had been put into the salad cooler at 9 am they were instructed to discarded all TCS foods at 1 pm. The salad bar only stays open until 4 pm, so all TCS foods will be discarded again when the salad bar closes. The deli PIC will be overseeing that time-as-control is correctly implemented. The store manager stated they will be scheduling maintenance for the salad cooler as soon as possible. Time-as-control must be used for all TCS foods until the salad cooler is properly functioning. The inspector will follow-up on 3/3/2025 to ensure that the salad cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed that the deli and meat department did not have sanitizer buckets available when the inspector arrived. Both PIC’s of the departments were educated that sanitizer buckets must be available during all hours of operation. Sanitizer buckets were filled in the deli and meat department during the inspection. Ensure that there is always saniztier available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the floors underneath the fryers in the deli have an accumulation of food debris and grease. The PIC was instructed to pull out the equipment and deep clean underneath the fryers by the next routine inspection. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed two half full cartons of milk in the walk-in cooler did not have date marking. The inspector discussed with the PIC who stated the milks were opened on Friday. The PIC correctly date marked the milks during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods held in the establishment for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed several single use articles stored on the floor in the hallway between the deli and the meat area. The boxes on the floor mostly consisted of to-go containers. There were some single-use articles stored on top of milk crates which is sufficient. Ensure that single use articles are stored at leases 6-inches above the ground. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
Observed a large leak coming from the faucet of the spray nozzle sink next to the fryers. Ensure that leak is fixed to maintain plumbing systems in good repair. The inspector will return on 09/20/2024 to check on the leak. 

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop stored with the head on the bottom of the mop sink. The mop was inverted during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
